generatedNotes: Legends re-tiers the whole Ranger book downward. In classic (P99) Rangers get their first spells at 9 and level in blocks (9/15/22/30/39/49/50+); on Legends the same spells appear from level 1 upward with per-level granularity. Level differences between `members[].level` (Legends, authoritative) and the classic level noted in `note` are therefore expected and systematic, not per-spell errors.

Legends also re-scales magnitudes: heals, DoTs and DD are markedly stronger than classic (e.g. Healing 135-175 vs classic 84-100; Stinging Swarm 27-42/tick vs classic 13/tick; Immolate 42-67/tick vs classic 24/tick), while AC on the coat line is slightly lower than classic.

Observed data-shape tell in the input file: effect strings phrased 'Increase Armor Class by N' carry Legends-tuned (usually lower) AC, while 'Increase AC by N' rows reproduce the classic P99 numbers verbatim. Every Skin-line spell appears TWICE in the file, once in each phrasing. See skin-line notes and openQuestions.

Stacking model used throughout: P99 Buff Lines groups every buff by the effect slot it writes to. 'Buffs under the same heading can't be stacked together.' Cross-line conflicts below are derived from shared headings/slots on that page.

replacement.note: Later members overwrite earlier ones (all write AC slot 1 and the HP Primary 'AC and HP' column, so only one can be up). BUT the chain is not monotonic in HP: Skin Like Rock scales to 105 max HP at L65 while Skin Like Steel caps at 100 max HP at L50. Above ~L50 a Ranger trades 5 max HP for 3-4 AC by moving from Rock to Steel. This quirk is classic and Legends reproduces it verbatim in both rows. Skin Like Diamond (200 HP) and Nature (250 HP) are unambiguous upgrades.

conflicts.detail: Courage, Center, Daring, Bravery, Valor, Resolution, Heroism and Fortitude all sit in AC slot 1 and in the same HP-Primary 'AC and HP' column as the Skin line. A cleric's Valor/Resolution/Heroism overwrites Skin Like Diamond/Nature and vice versa - only one lands.

Aegolism (Cleric 60) is the AC slot 1 & 4 combination buff: it blocks the Skin line AND the Aegis line at once. Per the page's own rule, a combination buff does not stack with the buffs listed underneath it.
Protection of the Glades (Druid 60, +24 AC / +470 HP) is the top of the same AC slot 1 / HP-Primary column. It overwrites any Skin-line buff on the Ranger.
Natureskin (Druid 57, +19 AC / +400 HP / +4 regen) is the Druid-only successor in the same slot; it replaces Skin Like Nature and also collides with Skin Like Nature's +2 regen in HP-Regen slot 4.
Inner Fire (Shaman 1, +3 AC / +20 HP) is in AC slot 1 - same line, blocked by any Skin buff.
Armor of Protection (Cleric 34) appears in the HP-Primary 'AC and HP' column (+225 HP), so it collides with the Skin line on HP even though its AC lives in slot 2.

Only for Skin Like Nature: its +2 HP/tick is HP-Regeneration slot 4, shared with Natureskin (+4) and the Rejuvenation potions (+10/+20/+40). A Rejuvenation potion will block or be blocked by Skin Like Nature's regen component.

stacksWith.detail: The Cleric Symbol line (Transal -> Ryltan -> Pinzarn -> Naltron -> Marzin, plus Naltron's Mark) is the separate 'HP Only and Requires Gem' column of HP (Primary). Per the page's column rule the two columns stack: Skin Like Nature + Symbol of Marzin both land. This is the standard Ranger buff pairing. Note the shared blocker: Aegolism combines both columns and therefore blocks both.
Cleric Holy Armor -> Guard -> Armor of Faith -> Shield of Words -> Aegis (and Bulwark of Faith) are AC slot 4; the Skin line is AC slot 1. They stack. Only Aegolism (slot 1 & 4) breaks this.

Shaman Talisman of Tnarg/Altuna/Kragg and the caster Shielding line are the separate 'HP (Shielding / Talisman)' heading; they stack with Skin-line HP. Focus of Spirit (Shaman 60) is explicitly exempted from the combination-blocking rule on that page.
Thistlecoat/Barbcoat/Bramblecoat/Spikecoat/Thorncoat are AC slot 2 - stack with the Skin line.
Riftwind's Protection / Call of Earth are AC slot 3 - stack with the Skin line.
Strength of Nature's +75 max HP is the 'HP (Strength)' heading, separate from HP (Primary) - it stacks with Skin-line HP. See the caveat in atk-self-line about its stacking block.

stacking.notes: The Ranger's ceiling stack is Skin Like Nature (AC1/HP) + Symbol of Marzin (HP) + Aegis/Bulwark (AC4) + a coat (AC2) + Call of Earth (AC3) + a Talisman/Shielding (HP). Accepting a cleric Heroism or an Aegolism replaces the Skin buff rather than adding to it.

members.note: Classic Druid 29 / Ranger 49. -10 to -18 AC plus a large fire DoT. Legends 42-67/tick vs classic 24/tick.

members.name: Stinging Swarm
members.note: Classic Druid 14 / Ranger 30. Legends 27-42/tick vs classic 13/tick.

members.name: Swarm of Pain
members.note: Post-classic - not on the P99 Ranger or Druid lists. 50-56/tick on Legends.

members.name: Drones of Doom
members.note: Classic Druid 34 / Ranger 54. Legends 148-156/tick vs classic 34/tick.

replacement.note: Monotonic damage; same DoT family so the later member overwrites the earlier on a target.

conflicts.detail: Members of this line overwrite each other on a target; a second Ranger casting a lower member wipes the higher one.

stacksWith.detail: Different DoT family - Immolate and Drones of Doom run together.

stacking.notes: These DoTs draw aggro on landing and each tick; the classic Ranger root-rot pattern is root + Immolate + Drones.

replacement.note: Straight damage upgrade against Construct/Elemental targets.

stacking.notes: Rangers stop at Dismiss Summoned in classic; the higher members are Druid-only, so the Legends omission is correct, not a gap.

members.name: Jolt

members.name: Cinder Jolt

stacking.notes: MISSING ON LEGENDS: Nullify Magic is a classic Ranger 58 spell (P99 Ranger/Spells, Kunark era; also Druid 44). Its absence leaves the Legends Ranger with only single-attempt dispel at level 60.

replacement.note: Larger stamina recovery; same effect.

stacking.notes: Effectively obsolete once stamina stopped gating melee, but classic-accurate.

unlinked.info: MISSING ON LEGENDS - Chloroplast. Classic Ranger 55 (also Druid 44, Shaman 39): +10 HP/tick regeneration, HP-Regeneration slot 1. Its absence means the Legends Ranger has NO regeneration buff at all except the incidental +2/tick rider on Skin Like Nature (which is regen slot 4, not slot 1). This is the single largest capability gap versus the classic Ranger.
MISSING ON LEGENDS - Nullify Magic. Classic Ranger 58 (Kunark), Cancel Magic (4). Leaves the Legends Ranger with only the level-30 single-attempt Cancel Magic.

HP-Regeneration slot 1 (Chloroplast, Regeneration, Regrowth, Regrowth of the Grove, Fungal Regrowth) is a separate heading from HP-Regeneration slot 4 (Skin Like Nature's +2, Natureskin's +4, the Rejuvenation potions). So a Fungi Staff or a druid's Regrowth stacks with Skin Like Nature's regen rider, but a Rejuvenation potion does not.

P99 internal inconsistency worth recording: the Ranger/Spells page omits Spikecoat from its level 49 block, but the Buff Lines page lists 'Spikecoat (Self-only: Druid 39, Ranger 49)' in both AC slot 2 and Damage Shield slot 3. Spikecoat IS a classic Ranger spell; Legends has it at 42.
P99 internal inconsistency: Endure Cold and Resist Cold are listed as Ranger 22 and Ranger 55 (Velious era) on Ranger/Spells but as Ranger 9 and Ranger 49 on Buff Lines. Legends uses 18 and 55.

Classic applies a hybrid-class penalty to some Ranger casts - P99 records Greater Healing as '288 (L24) to 300 (L30) (Hybrid Classes: 244 to 270 HP)'. This is the most likely explanation for the paired Skin-line rows in the Legends file, where one row carries lower AC than the other.
Rangers have no haste spell in any era, so the shaman/enchanter Haste (Primary) line and the Ervaj/v2 line never conflict with anything a Ranger casts.

Aegolism (Cleric 60) is the only buff that occupies AC slot 1 AND slot 4 simultaneously; it therefore blocks the Ranger's Skin line and the cleric Aegis line at once, and per the P99 max-HP table it is a net -70 HP versus the best mixed stack. A Ranger being buffed by a full cleric should prefer Heroism + Aegis + Symbol over Aegolism where the choice exists.

openQuestions: Every Skin-line spell appears TWICE in the Legends file - once with 'Increase Armor Class by N' (lower AC, level equal or 1-2 lower, targetType 'Single Friendly (or Self)') and once with 'Increase AC by N' (exactly the classic P99 values and the classic Ranger level, targetType 'Single'). Are these two distinct castable spells on Legends, a hybrid-penalty variant pair, or duplicated DB rows that should be de-duplicated before display? Same question for the AC phrasing on Riftwind's Protection, the coat line and Call of Earth.

Legends' Riftwind's Protection grants +30 AC while the level-48 Call of Earth grants only +20 AC (live EQ has 11-12 and 24-25 respectively). Is the +30 intentional, and does Call of Earth actually overwrite it in-game? If it does, the level-48 spell is an AC downgrade.

Force of Nature (L50) grants +5 damage shield and +6 HP/tick - which damage-shield slot and which regen slot? If its DS is slot 1 it conflicts with Shield of Spikes; if slot 3 it conflicts with the coat line. If its regen is slot 1 it partly replaces the missing Chloroplast.

Does casting Strength of Nature's 'Block new spell if slot 4 is effect Max Hitpoints and < 400' fire on Legends? If so, Rangers must be told to accept cleric/Skin HP buffs BEFORE self-casting Strength of Nature.
Do Spirit of the Shrew / Pack Shrew's Ultravision and Chill Sight's Ultravision overwrite each other on Legends?
Are added-melee-proc buffs (Call of Sky, Call of Fire) mutually exclusive with each other and with other proc buffs on Legends? No classic-source table covers proc buffs.
Legends' Ensnare is the same -40% as Snare (duration upgrade only). Intentional re-tier or a data error?

Our wiki mirror anchors a 'Blessing of the Page line' and a 'Shielding line'. Neither appears on the P99 AC/HP tables under those names (Shielding maps to the caster AC-slot-2 / HP-Shielding-Talisman entries). Confirm against the mirror whether Blessing of the Page shares a slot with the Skin line before publishing Ranger stacking advice.

Four spells in the file have no classic-era counterpart at all and should be confirmed as Legends-authored rather than mis-transcribed: Tangling Weeds, Hawk Eye, Harmony of Nature, Swarm of Pain (plus Nature's Precision and Force of Nature, which are named like later-era live spells).

members.name: Talisman of Tnarg
members.note: P99 classic level 34; Legends re-tiers to 32. +150 max HP classic vs 134-150 on Legends.

members.name: Talisman of Altuna
members.note: P99 classic level 44; Legends re-tiers to 40.

members.name: Focus of Spirit
members.note: Combination buff: its HP component sits IN this line (does not stack with Talisman of Kragg), but its STR/DEX components are separate lines that DO stack with the shaman STR/DEX primary lines.

replacement.note: Strictly increasing max-HP within the line (Legends: 150 -> 250 -> 380 -> 405), and all four occupy the same buff slot, so the later member always replaces the earlier. The only nuance is Focus of Spirit: you take it over Talisman of Kragg for HP, and it additionally carries STR/DEX that Kragg does not.

Cleric 34 self-only buff is listed in the same "HP (Shielding / Talisman)" heading (+225 HP) and therefore does not stack with the Talisman line.

stacksWith.detail: Druid/Ranger line shares the Heroism column, not the Talisman column, so it stacks with Talisman.

unlinked.info: Buff-line stacking on P99 is expressed as numbered effect SLOTS, not as named lines. Two buffs conflict if and only if they appear under the same slot heading. This is why the shaman AC line (AC Slot 4) collides with the cleric Aegis line but not the cleric Heroism line (AC Slot 1), and why Aegolism blocks BOTH (it occupies slots 1 and 4).

The whole-game HP ceiling is +1775 = Protection of the Glades (+470, druid AC-and-HP column) + Symbol of Marzin (+700, cleric HP-only column) + Focus of Spirit (+405, shaman Talisman/Shielding column) + Divine Strength (+200, paladin column). Four different columns, one from the shaman. This single row proves the Talisman line stacks with both cleric HP lines.

The shaman strength ceiling is +240 = Maniacal Strength (+68) + Focus of Spirit (+67) + Voice of the Berserker (+85) + Primal Essence (+20). Shamans cannot use bard Anthem songs on themselves for the Anthem column, which is why their max is 43 lower than a bard's +313.

Focus of Spirit is the ONLY spell P99 exempts from its own combination rule: "If a buff (except Focus of Spirit) combines multiple lines they will be listed below it in separate columns. The combination buffs won't stack with the buffs underneath." Focus of Spirit's HP does not stack with the Talisman line, but its STR and DEX are treated as separate lines that DO stack with the shaman stat buffs.

Cross-class regen: shaman Regeneration/Chloroplast/Regrowth are literally the same spells the druid gets (at different levels), all in HP Regeneration Slot 1. A Fungi Covered Great Staff click (+15) ties Regrowth, so in the classic era the fungi staff made shaman regen redundant on anyone who owned one.
Item-worn regeneration stacks with spell regeneration but has its own combined cap of +15 HP/tick across all worn sources.
Enchanter Tashan-line resist debuffs are unresistible and stack with the shaman Malo line; the canonical raid order is Tashan, then Malo (unresistible), then Malosini (resistible, larger).
Bard songs count against the same 15-buff limit as spells, so a shaman group-buffing into a bard group can push useful buffs off.

P99 Healing Spell Lines notes that Inner Fire is more mana-efficient per HP than Minor Healing, Light Healing, Healing OR Greater Healing — the shaman "buff heal" beats their own direct heals for a long stretch of levels.
Quiescence is the post-classic continuation of the Torpor line and, unlike Stoicism and Torpor, carries no snare or slow rider. It is absent from the Legends list.

openQuestions: Legends re-tiers roughly two thirds of the shaman book downward by 1-5 levels versus P99 classic (e.g. Talisman of Tnarg 34->32, Talisman of Altuna 44->40, Superior Healing 51->45, Cannibalize 34->23). The Talisman/Kragg, Deliriously Nimble, Talisman of the Cat/Brute/Rhino/Serpent/Raptor, Regrowth, Stoicism, Torpor and Celerity levels match classic exactly. Is the downward shift a deliberate levelling-curve change, or does it need auditing spell by spell?

Is the snare-HoT line (Snails / Tortoises / Slugs / Sloths Healing) confirmed Legends-custom? The Legends patch notes call Snails, Slugs and Sloths Healing new shaman spells and "alternatives to Rancor and Stoicism", but Tortoises Healing is not named in the notes I could reach, and gnollguard.com returned 403 to direct fetching.

Are Impassivity (16) and Nonchalance (30) real EQ spells or Legends-added lower tiers of the Torpor line? Stoicism (44) and Torpor (60) are both verified classic at exactly those levels, which makes two new tiers underneath look like a deliberate Legends addition.
Talisman of the Beast (level 8, GROUP +10 STR) appears in no classic source. Is it a Legends-added group Strengthen?
Insidious Decay (52) shows a WEAKER disease-resist debuff on Legends (-36 to -42) than Insidious Malady (38) does (-49 to -60). On live EQ the ordering is reversed. Data bug or deliberate re-tune?
Remove Curse (38) removes the same 4 curse counters as Remove Lesser Curse (24) in the Legends data. Probable magnitude bug.
Instill (33) has NO effects array in the Legends file. Allakhazam confirms it is a root-line spell of roughly double Root's duration; the effect data appears to be missing entirely.
Odium (43) lists only "Increase Curse Counter by 8" with no damage component, while Curse (34) does 148/tick. Is the DoT effect missing from the record?

The file contains three duplicate/near-duplicate records: Burst of Flame appears twice identically at level 1; Invisibility versus Animals appears twice at level 10 differing only in capitalisation and duration text; Turgur's Insects appears twice at level 51 differing only in the apostrophe character. These are 3 of the 209 rows and should probably be de-duplicated in the database.
Mass Imbue Sapphire is absent while the other four gems have both single and Mass variants, and Mass Imbue Ivory's effect string wrongly reads "Summon Item: Imbued Amber".
Spirit of Cheetah is a DRUID 60 self-only spell on P99 (+115%, 8 ticks). Legends gives it to Shaman at level 21 at +75%. Deliberate class re-assignment or a class-flag error?

unlinked.info: Buff-slot model that drives every stacking answer above: HP/AC buffs are grouped into columns - 'Primary (AC and HP)' = Courage/Heroism + Skin + Inner Fire + Protection of the Glades; 'Primary (HP-only, requires gem)' = Symbol line; 'Shielding / Talisman' = Shaman Talisman + int-caster Shielding + Armor of Protection; 'HP (Strength)' = Divine Vigor/Glory/Strength + Ranger Strength of Nature. Buffs under the same heading cannot stack; combination buffs (Aegolism) block every column they combine.

AC is slotted separately from HP: AC slot 1 = Courage/Heroism + Skin lines; AC slot 2 = Yaulp + int-caster Shielding + druid/ranger coat line + Armor of Protection; AC slot 3 = Call of Earth, Augment/Augmentation, Frenzy; AC slot 4 = Aegis line (incl. Spirit Armor) + Shaman Guardian line + Enchanter Shield line + Magician Phantom line. A Paladin can therefore run Courage-line AC and Aegis-line AC and Yaulp AC simultaneously - three separate AC slots.

Aegolism's implementation is a hard block, not a comparison: 'Block new spell if slot 3 is effect Max Hitpoints and < 1100'. That is why an Aegolism'd target refuses Symbol buffs and Protection of the Glades.

'Blessing of the Page' / 'Blessing of the Squire' (named in the anchor set) are not Paladin spells - on Legends they are Cleric spells (Blessing of the Squire = Cleric 16, a heal-proc buff). No member of that line appears in the Paladin file, so it is not tagged here.

Live-era Paladin spells inside Legends' level range that are absent from the Legends Paladin list and whose line membership could not be verified: Salve (1), Light of Life (52), Force of Akera (53), Quellious' Word of Tranquility (54), Austerity (55, described as an HP and AC buff - probably a Courage-line member between Valor and Resolution), Holy Aura (55), Breath of Tunare (56), Guard of Piety (56), Blessing of Austerity (58).

Paladin disciplines on live (Resistant 51, Fearless 54, Holyforge 55, Deflection 59, Sanctification 60) are not spells and are correctly absent from a spell table; noted only so their absence is not mistaken for a gap.

Level offsets: Legends' Paladin levels match the live Allakhazam Paladin list almost exactly (Cease 7, Desist 13, Reanimation 22, Divine Vigor 35, Wave of Life 39, Valor of Marr 44, Thunder of Karana 47, Brell's Steadfast Aegis 49, Instill 54, Improved Invis to Undead 63), NOT the P99 classic list, which is 2-9 levels later on almost every shared spell. Legends is best modelled as the post-classic Paladin list truncated near 63.

General rule for Paladins buffing in a mixed group: cast Symbol (HP-only slot) and Aegis-line AC freely; do not cast Courage-line buffs over a Druid/Ranger Skin buff or a Shaman's Inner Fire, and never over Protection of the Glades or Aegolism.

unlinked.info: THE MASTER STACKING RULE. p99 Buff Lines states it plainly: "Buffs under the same heading can't be stacked together. If a buff (except Focus of Spirit) combines multiple lines they will be listed below it in separate columns. The combination buffs won't stack with the buffs underneath, and those buffs will only stack with the other columns." Every conflict below is derived from which heading a spell appears under.

AC SLOT MAP relevant to a cleric-buffed character. Slot 1: Heroism line + druid/ranger Skin line + Protection of the Glades + Natureskin + shaman Inner Fire. Slot 2: caster Shielding line + cleric Yaulp I-IV + cleric Armor of Protection + druid/ranger coat line (Thistlecoat->Thorncoat) + magician Phantom line is actually slot 4. Slot 3: Ranger Call of Earth, enchanter Augmentation/Augment, shaman Frenzy. Slot 4: cleric Aegis line + shaman Guardian/Shroud of the Spirits + enchanter Umbra/Shadow + magician Phantom Armor. Aegolism uniquely occupies Slot 1 AND Slot 4.

HP COLUMN MAP. HP (Primary) has three parts: the combination row (Aegolism, +1100), the "AC and HP" column (Protection of the Glades +470, Heroic Bond +400, Heroism +400, Natureskin +400, Fortitude +345, Resolution +250, Skin Like Nature +250, Armor of Protection +225, Skin Like Diamond +200, Valor +200, Bravery +140, Skin Like Steel +100, Skin Like Rock +100, Center +95, Courage +20, Skin Like Wood +20, Inner Fire +20), and the "HP Only and Requires Gem" column (Symbol of Marzin +700, Symbol of Naltron +525, Naltron's Mark +446, Symbol of Pinzarn +307, Symbol of Ryltan +158, Symbol of Transal +73). A separate heading, HP (Shielding / Talisman), holds Focus of Spirit +405, Talisman of Kragg +380, Shield of the Magi +250, Talisman of Altuna +250, Armor of Protection +225, Arch Shielding +150, Talisman of Tnarg +150 and the lower Shielding spells.

THE BEST CLASSIC HP/AC STACK does NOT include Aegolism. Because Protection of the Glades (Skin/Heroism column) stacks with Symbol of Marzin (Symbol column) and with Bulwark of Faith (AC slot 4), a group with a level 60 druid and a level 57+ cleric gets 470 + 700 = 1170 HP and 24 + 37 = 61 AC plus 6 mana per tick, beating Aegolism's 1100 HP / 54 AC - and Aegolism would block PotG outright. The cleric should skip Aegolism and cast Symbol of Marzin + Bulwark of Faith on top of the druid's PotG.
Verbatim p99: "Aegolism and PotG do not stack with each other and neither will override the other." So a mis-timed Aegolism locks the group out of PotG for its full 2h30m.

Verbatim p99 on Aegolism: "For stacking purposes, this spell is considered an 'all-in-one' spell, replacing Heroism, Symbol of Marzin and Aegis with a single buff with roughly the same stats and reduced overall mana cost." And on its own page: "This buff will prevent PoTG from sticking."

The Legends Aegolism record carries the classic stacking blocker verbatim in its effects: "Stacking: Block new spell if slot 3 is effect 'Max Hitpoints' and < 1100". Symbol spells put Max Hitpoints in slot 3 (Allakhazam shows Symbol of Transal as "3: Increase Max Hitpoints"), which is the mechanism by which Aegolism refuses the Symbol line.

The DRUID SKIN LINE members, from the provided druid file and the p99 AC Slot 1 / HP Primary table: Skin Like Wood (1), Skin Like Rock (14), Skin Like Steel (24), Skin Like Diamond (36/39), Skin Like Nature (46/49), Natureskin (57), Protection of the Glades (60, group). Rangers share the line at higher levels (Skin Like Wood 9, Rock 22, Steel 39, Diamond 54, Nature 59). p99: "Druids and Rangers have access to this line of hit point and armor increasing buffs."

CLERIC vs DRUID AT COMPARABLE LEVELS (both files' own numbers, max-level values). L1 Courage 4 AC / 20 HP == Skin Like Wood 4 AC / 20 HP, tie. L7-16 Center 6 AC / 95 HP vs Skin Like Rock 7 AC / 105 HP - DRUID WINS this band. L17-23 Daring 9 AC / 130 HP vs Skin Like Rock - cleric wins. L22-31 Bravery 10 AC / 140 HP vs Skin Like Steel 10 AC / 100 HP - cleric wins. L32-41 Valor 13 AC / 200 HP vs Skin Like Diamond 13 AC / 200 HP - dead tie at cap, but the cleric gets it 4-7 levels earlier. L42-51 Resolution 16 AC / 250 HP vs Skin Like Nature 16 AC / 250 HP + 2 HP/tick - tie, druid adds regen. L52-59 Heroism 19 AC / 400 HP vs Natureskin 19 AC / 400 HP + 4 HP/tick - tie at cap, druid version arrives 5 levels later but adds regen. L60 Aegolism 54 AC / 1100 HP (single) vs Protection of the Glades 24 AC / 470 HP + 6 mana/tick (GROUP).

RESIST BUFF CEILING: the cleric line stops at +40 (Resist Fire/Cold/Poison/Disease/Magic). Druid Circle of Winter/Summer and shaman Talisman of Jasinth/Shadoo give +45 in the SAME primary slot, so a druid or shaman in group makes the cleric resist buffs redundant rather than additive.

Legends' cleric levels track the MODERN (post-revamp) Allakhazam level assignments, not the p99 classic ones. Examples: Holy Armor 1 (p99 5), Center 7 (p99 9), Daring 17 (p99 19), Bravery 22 (p99 24), Guard 25 (p99 29), Valor 32 (p99 34), Armor of Faith 35 (p99 39), Resolution 42 (p99 44), Shield of Words 45 (p99 49), Yaulp II 16 (p99 19), Yaulp III 41 (p99 44), Healing 10 (p99 14), Greater Healing 20 (p99 24), Superior Healing 30 (p99 34), Symbol of Naltron 41 (p99 44). Every one of these matches Allakhazam exactly. When annotating, use Allakhazam levels as the level authority and p99 only for line membership and stacking.

Spells present on Allakhazam's cleric list at level 60 and below but absent from Legends, beyond those noted per-line: the nine LDoN "Iony's" adventure utility spells (Lesser/normal/Greater Augury, Exorcism and Cleansing at 10/14/23/24/33/34), Epitaph of Life 52, Mark of Retribution 54, Aura of the Zealot 55, Ethereal Light 58, Blessed Armor of the Risen 58, Ethereal Remedy 59, Imbue Valor 59, Deistic Voice 59, Ancient High Priest's Bulwark 60, Ancient Gift of Aegolism 60, Blessing of Aegolism 60, Ethereal Elixir 60, Marzin's Mark 60. All are LDoN-or-later, so their absence is consistent with a classic-through-Velious spell set.

Lines with NO classic counterpart at all (Legends originals): the Echo line (Echo of Health / Echoing Light / Renewing Echo / Celestial Echo / Sacred Echo) and the Blessing of the Page proc-heal line (Page / Squire / Knight / Lord Commander). Neither name set appears on Allakhazam or p99.

openQuestions: p99 Buff Lines lists Armor of Protection's +225 HP under BOTH the Heroism/Skin column of HP (Primary) and under HP (Shielding / Talisman). Which is right decides whether a cleric self-buffing Armor of Protection loses their Heroism-line HP or their shaman Talisman HP. The Shielding/Talisman placement is more consistent with its AC Slot 2 assignment.
Armor of the Faithful (49) is on Allakhazam but on none of the p99 stacking tables, so its AC and HP slot assignments are unknown. Does it conflict with Armor of Protection, or with the Heroism line?

Legends Temperance (40) and Blessing of Temperance (45) give +800 max HP and +160 AC - values with no classic analogue at any level. Which slots do they occupy on Legends, and do they block Aegolism / PotG?
Turning of the Unnatural (37) does 25 HP/tick against Sermon of the Righteous (25) at 69-79 HP/tick. Is the Legends magnitude wrong, or are the two genuinely not one line?

Several detrimental spells quote damage at level bands far below their own spell level (Ward Summoned 17 "6 (L2) to 14 (L18)", Expulse Summoned 27 "113 (L13)", Earthquake 44 "214 (L31)", Upheaval 52 "618 (L48)", Banish Summoned 56 "529 (L43)"). Is that a scraping artefact or the real Legends scaling?
Symbol of Naltron and Naltron's Mark both carry "UNKNOWN CALC 118" in the Legends effects. p99 resolves them to +525 and +446 max HP - should those be backfilled?

Four records look like duplicates: Invisibility versus Undead / Invisibility Versus Undead (both 11), Improved Invisibility to Undead (48) / Improved Invis vs Undead (50), and two identical Imbue Emerald (29). Deduping would take the cleric list from 206 to 203.
